newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal 97 budget proposal sees corporate tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Portugal 97 budget proposal sees corporate tax cut.

text.p: The Portuguese government's 1997 budget proposals include a reduction in corporate tax of up to two percentage points to 34 percent, Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said.
"The corporate tax rate will fall by up to two percentage points in 1997," Sousa Franco said during a meeting to present the government's budget proposals to opposition parties.
Presently the corporate tax rate is 36 percent.
Sousa Franco said the government planned to adjust income tax bands next year for the highest paid tax payers by 2.5 percent and the lowest tax payers by up to four percent.
The government's 1997 budget proposals forecast a budget deficit of 2.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product and inflation of between 2.25 and 2.5 percent.
The government is due to present its budget proposals to parliament on October 15. Analysts expect it to be passed in a vote in November.
